verdicts.summary:
Explore direction: Linear's classic two-pane frame, laid flush, more compact, with each theme's accent in the frame.
- The inset rounded main sheet is gone. The main column is now the page itself at full height. The sidebar is a tinted rail (232px), separated from the page by one hairline (--side-edge). The --panel-ring token is removed from every theme.
- The sidebar is denser: 13px medium labels on 28px rows, 1px between rows and 20px between groups. Section headings are 12px muted. The head buttons are 24px and the head stays level with the page's top bar.
- Colour: the Space tile uses the theme's accent (--you). The current view is a pill tinted with --you, and its glyph is lit in --you (--you-text in dark themes; new token --side-on-glyph). So the frame shows which theme is on.
- View counts are now plain muted numbers instead of white boxed badges. This removes the --side-count-fill, --side-count-ring, --side-count, --side-count-on and --side-count-h tokens.
- The theme row matches the compact rows (13px label, 12px current theme name). The theme menu swatches are larger (38x24) and redrawn as the new frame in miniature: the rail with its accent tile, a hairline, then the page with a line of ink and a line of your move.
- Theme tokens are reworked for the rail: Paper 4% ink, dark themes 22% black under the page, accent-tinted active pills. Token comments now say rail and page instead of sheet, and the Frame ledger reasons are updated (flush main column, muted numeral counts).
- Kit size went down: 8339 lines in all, under the starting size. No components, props, budget or raises were changed.

In dark mode the same tints turn into muddy brown and maroon bars. The 'Retry' button is still grey-filled next to white 'Request changes' buttons. The avatar initials in the card status pills are still about 6px and unreadable. In the dark expanded run, the stepper still shows an empty segment above 'Lint / Skipped'. verdicts.summary:
Explore direction "status-washed sheet". Each group's band is now tinted with its state's colour, so where each run of tickets starts is shown by colour rather than lines.
- Group heads (Head): the band takes a light wash of the group's state colour: indigo for Needs you / Your move, orange for Running / Agents at work, red for Blocked, green for Done. Neutral groups use a lighter ink wash. The count is written in the same colour, the name is weight 600, and the hairline under the band is gone. Two new tones (live, blocked) were added to Head and to Badge's count. CompactView maps each group to its tone, and QueueView sets Agents at work to live. The bands are built from new tokens (--band-tint per theme, plus --band-ink/you/live/blocked/done mixed from the base colours).
- Rows (Row line): density goes from 44px to 40px (--h-line), with no separators between rows; the group bands do that job. Hover, focus and the open row now show a rounded slab inset 6px from the edges. In Compact the open row's expansion sits inside the slab, washed in your accent. Item rows (Intake) keep their hairline.
- Chips: flat tags with a faint ink fill, no outline, 6px radius, 20px tall (was 22). The tokens header already said "borders are for controls", and this now matches it. The fill tone is one step firmer.
- Agents at work tiles (Card agent look): running tiles are flat grey slabs with no border or shadow. Queued tiles are an empty dashed outline, matching the dashed queued glyph. The Meter's bottom-edge hairline (size edge) is replaced by size tile: a still, 76px segmented meter set inline before the step count.
- Cleanup: removed the tokens nothing uses any more (--list-label-edge, --tile-meter-track, --tile-quiet-edge, --tile-bar). Updated the ledger entries and source comments for Head, Badge, Chip, Meter, Row and Card so they stay true.
Kit: 8,363 lines before, 8,380 after (+17 net), 44/45 components; "budget" and "raises" untouched.
Environment note: in this worktree the node_modules junction made Vite return 403 for the Geist font files, so pages rendered in a fallback font. To shoot with the real font, I made web\node_modules a real folder holding junctions to each package plus a real copy of @fontsource. This changed only the worktree, not C:\code\AgentOS-V2-web, and isn't part of the patch. The final shots are in Geist.

verdicts.summary:
The challenger rebuilds All teams as Linear's swimlane board.
- **Repo heads.** The left "Team" column is gone. Each repo gets one head line across the full board: name, in-flight count, path, coloured people faces, and "Open list →" at the far right. The four stage lanes now use the whole width.
- **Wells.** Each stage lane in a swimlane is a rounded well set a step into the sheet: a grey well with an inner hairline in light, a black-mixed well in dark. The white or lit cards stand out of it. An empty lane stays a bare well, so the board's shape shows. A repo with nothing in flight gets one quiet full-width well.
- **Spacing.** Swimlanes are separated by space instead of hairline rules. Column heads are inset to line up with the card keys.
- **Cards.** Cards drop from three lines to two, like Linear's board card: the key and the state chip on one line (chip at the far end), then the status glyph and the title in 13px medium.
- **Kit changes.** Row gets a `head` prop (rendered for bands), and the band CSS is rewritten. The ticket Card's main area stretches so its line reaches the card's far edge. Two new tokens (`--lane-well`, `--lane-well-edge`) are mixed from the base tokens in the light and dark blocks; the unused `--h-band` is removed. The ledger entries for Row (band, head) and Card ticket are updated.
- **Budget.** The kit grows by 17 lines net (8363 to 8380). Components stay at 44/45; budget and raises are unchanged.

To make the shots, I temporarily added `server.fs.allow` to `web/vite.config.ts`. Without it, Vite refuses to serve the Geist fonts through the junctioned `node_modules` and the shots fall back to a system font. That change is reverted and is not in the patch. Other builders' shots from junctioned worktrees will likely show the wrong font for the same reason.

Note: the camera writes into a `teams` subfolder of the given output folder.

verdicts.summary:
The challenger restyles the overlays as a "docked sheet plus window chrome" family. It changes the chrome only and adds no feature or data.

Peek:
- It is docked full height, flush to the right edge, instead of a floating card. It has a hairline on its left edge and a long side shadow (new token --shadow-dock).
- The list beside it is lightly veiled rather than dimmed (new token --tk-veil), so it stays readable.
- A new pinned bar (Dialog's new `bar` prop, side look only) holds the type glyph and key on the left, then a quiet Open ticket, the ticket menu and a quiet close. Its hairline sits on the same line where the page's own top bar ends (h-top + sp-4), so the two read as one bar across the window.
- The title is now 24px display, matching the ticket page. Text's unused "title" variant is removed, which saves kit lines.
- The panel's Sections are set apart by space instead of hairlines, so the peek reads as one document (like Linear's doc page) between its pinned bar and its pinned composer.

Full-window editors (workflow overlay and item overlay):
- The editor is the app's main sheet lifted over the window: inset sp-4 and corner r-4, the same as the frame's sheet, with a deeper --shadow-float on the scrim.
- The bar is a window chrome: the close, then a short vertical rule, then the Page's top bar. One hairline runs edge to edge under all of it, so it no longer stops at the close's column.

Ledger entries updated: Dialog (`bar` prop and both look values), Text (`display` now covers the peek; `title` removed) and Section's reason. The kit sheet's list of Text variants is updated to match. The kit is at 8,383 of 9,000 lines (44/45 components), about +23 net.

verdicts.summary:

- Item editors (agent, skill, file, and a ticket's copy): the name is an unboxed 24px title (a file's path stays monospace) and the description is an unboxed 16px lead ("Add a short summary…"). There are no Name or Description label rows any more. The instructions, SKILL.md or file text is the page's own monospace text with no box; it has a focus ring and still pops out to a boxed full-window editor. Each AGENTS.md block is a section of the document: its name is an unboxed 15px heading, and the line count, a caret fold and move up/down sit at the right. The body text lines up with the heading.
- Side rail: runtime, model and effort are Linear property chips (no box until hovered), with their words lined up with the plain values beside them. Select's unused "field" look is removed to pay for this.

One continuous axis runs down the lane through every face; the faces knock it out, and it ends at the last joint, or at the last face when read-only. The selected stage rises onto a raised card ringed in the accent. The loop is an edgeless wash. "Every stage gets" is an unboxed line above the lane. Library palette items are bare list rows instead of small cards.
- Kit cost is +16 lines net (8,363 to 8,379), with no new components. Two props were added and recorded in the ledger: Field.look (title, lead, heading) and TextArea.bare. verdicts.summary:

verdicts.summary:
The direction follows Linear's Ash theme: neutral bands, rows on hairlines and outlined pill chips.
- Group and zone heads: the per-status band tints are gone. Every group, Agents at work included, now sits on one neutral grey band (--list-band). The status shows only in the head's coloured glyph and its coloured count. The name is ink at weight 500. In dark mode this ends the brown and maroon bars. The tint tokens (--band-*, --band-tint, --list-band-ink) and Head's data-tone rules are deleted.
- Rows: Row line is now a flat row running edge to edge on a hairline, as in Linear's list, 42px tall instead of 40. The hover and open wash fill the whole width instead of a rounded slab held in from the edges.
- Chips: inside a list row or an agent tile, a label chip is a pill on a hairline with no fill. This is scoped by the row's data-row attribute and the tile's data-look="agent", so chips on other screens are unchanged. Keycaps pick up the same hairline.
- Agents at work: running and queued tiles now look the same, the surface on a hairline using the existing --tile tokens. The dashed card and the grey slab are both gone, so the dashed glyph alone says queued. The owner's face has moved out of the pill and is drawn at row size (18px), which fixes the 6px initials. The pill keeps the agent's words and its glyph on the live disc. Card's agent `off` prop is removed.
- Retry: the ink button is now the default white fill with a firmer edge and weight, so it matches the Request changes buttons next to it. The unused --ctl-strong tokens are deleted.
- Stepper: --tk-skip was only defined for the light themes, so in dark mode the skipped Lint stage drew an empty segment. The token moved to the block every theme shares, and the dashes now show in dark.
- Ledger entries for Head tone, Row line, Chip (why, line, fill), Card (off, agent look) and Button ink are updated to match. Kit lines went from 8,496 to 8,458 (net -38). Components stay at 44 of 45. Budget and raises are untouched.

verdicts.gap: Collapse the stacked right column (ID over time) into one line, or move the ID into the meta line, and cut the row height from about 74px to about 52px. Each row is currently two lines tall on both sides, which halves density and makes the list feel padded.
verdicts.problems: The 16px avatar initials in the meta line ('BQ', 'CR', 'DS') are too small to read, especially in dark. verdicts.summary:

verdicts.summary:
Direction: one family of sheets lifted over a scrim, and one aligned left edge in place of boxes. The full-window item editor is now a centred document, like Linear's project page.

It floats inset by --sp-4 with rounded corners and the float shadow, over the same --tk-scrim as the full overlays, so the queue is dimmed (the veil is gone). The bar and foot have no rules. I built the frame challenger as one bold direction: Linear's classic Ash/Midnight frame instead of the current inset sheet. It removes one of the two nested frames, which was the critic's biggest gap.

The queue's bordered list card is gone, so the bands and rows sit straight on the page, as Linear's lists do. Compact and the kit sheet get the same treatment, and the dead strip inside the old panel is gone too.

This replaces the old per-theme sidebar colours and `--panel-ring` shadows in Carbon, Midnight, Harbour and Plum. Paper's ground is lightened to 4% ink. Mist is now literally Ash: a white page and a cool blue-grey sidebar (`#edeef3`).

The kit is 47 lines smaller than the base.

How it works: in web/src/kit/TextArea.tsx, any text area with a head strip (the item editor's content: AGENTS.md blocks, an agent's instructions, a SKILL.md) stacks a rendered layer over its textarea in one grid cell. The rendered layer is hidden from screen readers and lets clicks through. At rest the textarea's text is transparent, so you see the rendered layer. A click lands in the source at roughly that spot. While the textarea has focus the rendered layer hides and you edit the raw source in place. On blur it reads formatted again.

The renderer is about 20 lines and handles paragraphs, `-`/`*` lists, `#` headings, ``` fences, `code` and **strong**. The CSS is in Form.module.css (.read and .prose) and uses existing tokens only (--chip-hover, --fs-tk, --font-mono), so there are no new colours. `.sheet:has(> .leaf:focus)` became `.sheet:has(.leaf:focus)` so the lit hairline still works inside the new wrapper. The same rendering also shows in the library's editors, because they use the same item editor. A separate click-through run (scratchpad\g2\ovtest) checked that clicking edits the source, Unsaved changes appears, and blur goes back to the formatted view.
